newsitem.title: USA: Fed must stay vigilant against inflation-McDonough.
newsitem.headline: Fed must stay vigilant against inflation-McDonough.

text.p: President of the New York Federal Reserve Bank William McDonough said he is pleased with the cyclical performance of the U.S. economy and the tame inflation picture, but said the Fed must remain vigilant against incipient signs of inflation.

Speaking to a group of business leaders in Rochester, New York, McDonough said the underlying fundamentals of the economy, namely consumer, business, and financial balance sheets, remain "vastly improved" from where they were in the late 1980s.

"The unemployment rate is around 5.5 percent, which most economists would agree is close to full employment," McDonough said in prepared remarks, a copy of which were released here. "In fact, it has been below 6.0 percent for over two years."

Last Friday, the Labor Department released its August employment report, which showed the jobless rate collapsed to 5.1 percent, the lowest in over seven years. It also said 250,000 new jobs were created in the month and wages shot up.
McDonough said the inflation story "also has been good," with the core Consumer Price Index (CPI) slowing to about 2.75 percent in the first half of 1996 from 3.0 percent.
Core CPI excludes volatile food and energy items.

As for the recent rise in wages, McDonough said: "Growth of wages has begun to increase somewhat recently, but in this era of global competition, there remains some question as to whether that will lead to a faster pace of price inflation.

"Indeed, recent experience suggests that it is difficult to predict the so-called 'natural rate' of unemployment associated with intensified inflationary pressures. There is no easily-seen red line that the economy should stay away from," he added.

McDonough said, however, that he disagrees with those economic forecasters who feel current well behaved prices mean Fed policymakers can ignore signs of intensified use of labor and capital resources.

"The Fed must remain vigilant with regard to incipient signs of inflation; it is clear that the failure to contain price inflation at its earliest stages only makes it more difficult and costlier to bring it under control later," he said.
